title: What is known about 1RB---_1RC0LE_1RD1RF_1LB0LB_0RD0LD_0RC0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1RC0LE_1RD1RF_1LB0LB_0RD0LD_0RC0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine moves material, one word every two visits, from one long run of a periodic word into another; each phase leaves a marker behind, and the runs it leaves have lengths in ratios close to 3/2, the usual sign of a Collatz-like map.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 73,042 cells have been visited and 40,382 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.444). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Transfer phases
claims.text: At the left-end visits in state D the first run loses one period-6 word and the second gains one period-9 word per round (750 per 1,500 rounds from 5.5·10<sup>8</sup> to 8.0·10<sup>8</sup> steps); the frozen runs to the right have lengths 133, 88, 58, 38, 15.

claims.title: Transfer phases
claims.text: At the left-end visits in state D the first run loses one period-6 word and the second gains one period-9 word every two visits (750 per 1,500 visits from 5.5·10<sup>8</sup> to 8.0·10<sup>8</sup> steps); the frozen runs to the right have lengths 133, 88, 58, 38, 15.

claims.title: Transfer phases
claims.text: At the left-end visits in state D the first run loses one period-6 word and the second gains one period-9 word every two visits (750 per 1,500 visits from 5.5·10<sup>8</sup> to 8.0·10<sup>8</sup> steps); the frozen runs to the right have lengths 133, 88, 58, 38, 15.

claims.title: No halt in the first 5.77×10<sup>10</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 5.77×1010 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 9 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

facts.text: between consecutive frozen runs: probably a Collatz-like map.
No halt in the C simulator; 73,042 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.00×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Moving material between runs
html: The tape is made of long runs of a few periodic words, mostly 100010000 (9 cells) and 000100 or 000001 (6 cells), separated by short markers. Every second time the head, in state D, comes back to the left end, one more word has moved from the first run to the next one: the first run shrinks by one word of 6 cells and the second grows by one word of 9 cells. When the first run is empty a new phase begins with other words.

Each phase leaves a marker and a run behind it. The runs further right are frozen; their lengths, 133, 88, 58, 38 and 15 for one kind of word, shrink by factors close to 3/2. That is how Collatz-like maps usually show up in these machines, but the exact map and its halting condition have not been worked out.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.444). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 73,042 cells (46,778 left of the start, 32 right), with a density of 1s of 0.553.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Phases of transfer between long runs of period-6 and period-9 words; the frozen runs it leaves behind shrink by ratios close to 3/2, the mark of a Collatz-like map (not extracted).
